Áelendi Language

Áelendi is the most conservative member of the entire Pelwar language family, preserved and spoken by the Áelendan people—the "People of the Covenant"—who dwell in the mountains of central Élavendre. The Áelendan consider themselves the guardians of an ancient compact with the land itself, and their language reflects this sacred role.

Áelendi Overview

Áelendi represents a direct descent from an ancient form of [[doc-pelwarpepl|Pelwar People]], preserved with minimal change over millennia. The Áelendan deliberately minimize linguistic change as a matter of cultural practice, viewing language change as a form of cultural loss. New concepts are incorporated through loan translation (creating new words from ancient roots) rather than loanwords.

Áelendi Phonology

Áelendi preserves a complex phonemic inventory lost in younger Pelwar languages:

Consonants: Áelendi distinguishes plain, aspirated, and ejective consonants for most stop consonants (t/th/t', d/dh/d', k/kh/k', g/gh/g'). These distinctions, which have merged or been abandoned in Élavendri proper, remain phonemic and meaningful. The language employs only one fricative (s) and one liquid of each type (l, r), with other Pelwar fricatives represented as secondary articulations of stops.

Vowels: Áelendi maintains eight vowel positions with clear length distinctions. The nasal vowels of Élavendri are not true phonemes in Áelendi but rather the result of n dropping out after a vowel. The vowel inventory is more stable and resistant to diphthongization than in Élavendri.

Stress: Stress consistently falls on the first syllable of roots, following a clear predictable pattern. This predictability, combined with conservative phonetics, makes Áelendi relatively easy to learn despite its phonetic complexity.

Áelendi Grammar

Word Order: Áelendi employs a rigid SOV word order that has remained constant throughout its history. Poetic reordering is permitted but rare and marked as archaic even in ancient poetry.

Noun Cases: Áelendi preserves a four-case system (nominative, accusative, genitive, locative), more than the three cases of Élavendri. Case marking is thorough and pervasive.

Gender: Áelendi maintains three genders (masculine, feminine, neuter) with consistent agreement patterns. The gender system correlates closely with semantic features (masculine = strength/light; feminine = growth/darkness; neuter = static/eternal).

Verbal System: Verbs employ both tense and aspect distinctions, resulting in a complex conjugation system. Strong verb forms are more numerous in Áelendi than in Élavendri, and the pattern of ablaut (vowel changes) follows predictable rules.

Articles: Áelendi employs a simpler article system than Élavendri, with only definite and indefinite forms. The demonstrative system is more elaborate, reflecting Áelendan concerns with spatial and temporal precision.

Áelendi Liturgical Role

While Áelendi is a living language among the Áelendan, it also serves a sacred function for the broader Élavendre realm. Magical texts of great antiquity are written in Áelendi, and scholars of magic often learn Áelendi specifically to read these texts in their original form. The language is used in the highest magical workings, as the Áelendan believe it carries greater power due to its connection to ancient covenant-making.

Mutual Intelligibility

An Élavendri speaker cannot understand Áelendi without study. The phonetic differences alone create comprehension barriers, and the grammatical divergences multiply the difficulty. However, shared roots and similar overall structure allow motivated learners to acquire Áelendi, and many educated Élavendri speakers maintain passive comprehension of at least formal Áelendi.

Áelendi speakers generally understand Élavendri quite well, having borrowed or kept many Élavendri innovations. Educated Áelendan often code-switch between Áelendi and Élavendri for pragmatic reasons.

Sample Phrases

  • "Al-síren ek dûl-thân, al-kír ek dûl-síl." – "Life flows from the deep dark, light rises from the deep-still." (Ancient creation phrase, perfectly balanced.)
  • "Ek-thalíren en símat dûl-el." – "The covenant holds through all time." (Oath formula.)
  • "Síres en thal-kír, síres en thal-dûn." – "The people of light, the people of darkness." (Archaic dualistic reference.)
